rationale: M60 #748 — the M49 dup-key family ruling (Option A) in python, in BOTH directions (a genuine rebinding collapses, a declaration chain does not). MEASURED before the change, range-keyed over python's two pinned corpora (cython 475 + requests 37 files): 25 duplicate-name scopes, of which only ONE is a genuine same-block rebinding — cython tests/run/class_scope.py MethodRedef.a, whose own docstring asserts the rule (`MethodRedef().a(5)` is 7 — the SECOND body wins). The other 24 split into 21 DECLARATION CHAINS (5 @overload groups in cython's Shadow.py, 9 in requests, 7 property-accessor chains) and 3 BRANCH ALTERNATIVES under `if/else` or `try/except/else` (Dependencies.record_results, runtests.skip_test, Pythran.pythran_is_numpy_func_supported) — exactly one of each pair runs, so neither may be dropped. Both of the last two are what a block-blind last-wins gets wrong, and it cost 2 real edges on cython before they were separated. requests has no genuine rebinding at all, and the corpus delta is 0 edges on both sides: the differential cannot score this rule, which is why a fixture has to hold it — in both directions. The blind-spot sweep found it (C4 class); only a fixture keeps it. Binding semantics: `def` is a binding statement and python binds the LAST definition of a name in one container scope — the earlier function object is rebound away before the module finishes executing, so its body can never run. The lane kept BOTH (a second symbol plus a call graph and a cyclomatic count split across a dead body). The ruling: ONE symbol per (container, name) keyed to the LAST declaration, phantom body edges dropped — the same contract js/ts/vue pinned for duplicate keys. Container identity is the scope NODE, not the class NAME: the sibling class D reuses `foo` freely (the W2/J3 identity ruling). Four independent passes are pinned, because a skipped subtree has to be skipped by every pass, not just the structural one: symbols (expectSymbolCount = 1, and expectSymbolRanges startLine at the WINNER's line, so a keep-both reading fails twice — once on the count, once on which def survived), the WINNER's edges (expectRelationships, with the M59 line of each), the phantom's body edges in three kinds (calls / uses / references, all forbid pins), and the file complexity (expectMetadata: the phantom's `if` is not a decision point of a file that cannot execute it). A result-transform mutant python/dupdef-keep-both re-injects the pre-fix observable (duplicate symbols, the phantom's three edges, complexity 2) and dies on every one of them.
